rem:qstar-decay-sector-q0:
Remark The S = 0 point q^{*} is conditional on c_3^{\mathrm{even}} = -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), not an independent determination of q_0. The bar-odd decay observable, taken here in its c_3-level normalization S(q) = c_3(q) + \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) (the same object as the preceding remark's \mathfrak{Q}_\beta/E_0 up to the ladder rescaling), is a deterministic function of the aether modulus: c_3(q) is the ladder extractor c_3 = (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta / Q_{N2} - 1)/u^3, where Q_{N2} is the c_2-level ladder truncation of \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, u = b\,\hbar_q^2, and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, m_e are fixed physical constants. Its zero is therefore root-found, not interpolated from anchors:

  q^{*} \approx 1.10997859303152\ldots,

the point where c_3 = -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) exactly — the pure bar-even aether point with vanishing decay projection (\varepsilon = \mathrm{Im}(q) = 0 in the reading of the interpreted conjecture's candidate (iii)). It lies \approx 80.3\% of the way from the proton anchor toward the muon anchor under the half-argument phase evaluation; see the parameter-sensitivity note below.

q^{*} is independent of both mass-sector pins — it uses neither m_\mathfrak{p} nor m_\mu — but it is not an independent third determination of q_0. Such a claim would be circular: q^{*} is defined above as the root of S(q) = c_3(q) + \mathrm{Vol}(4_1), so locating it presupposes c_3^{\mathrm{even}} = -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1). It is a determination of q_0 conditional on that hypothesis, which is precisely the hypothesis an independent determination would have to avoid.

The supporting statistics do not rescue it. At q^{*} the muon ratio m_\mu/m_e deviates \approx 42.7 ppb from CODATA, versus \approx 1.4 ppb at the muon anchor and \approx 211 ppb at the proton anchor; and q^{*} is indeed not the statistical reconciliation of the \mu–\mathfrak{p} tension (the precision-weighted mean sits \approx 0.0007\% muon-ward, essentially at the proton anchor, which is \approx 367\times more precise, while q^{*} sits 80.3\% muon-ward). Both remain true and neither is evidence, because the 80.3\% is a reading of \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)'s own value: every constant V in the window (-c_3(\mu), -c_3(\mathfrak{p})) = (2.0202,\, 2.0693) of width 0.0491 places a zero between the anchors, and as V sweeps that window the corresponding q^{*}_V sweeps the entire anchor interval. \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.0299 sits 80.30\% of the way from the proton end of that window, the same figure. Choosing a different in-window constant relocates q^{*} and would produce a different percentage, equally far from both pins and from their weighted mean.

The \mu–\mathfrak{p} aether tension is therefore two-way, holding between the two mass pins alone.

Parameter sensitivity. The placement of q^{*} between the anchors depends on the weight z entering the phase \alpha = (z-1)h/2 of the c_3 extractor. Setting z = 1/(\sqrt{q} + 1/\sqrt{q}) \approx 0.49932 gives \alpha \approx -0.052336, whereas the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) \approx 0.61269 gives \alpha \approx -0.040486, a 23\% shift. Root-finding the same extractor with only z changed yields:

q^3/(q^2+1) 1.11023370740\ldots outside it, by \approx 19{,}921 anchor-gaps

The anchor interval is only 1.281 \times 10^{-8} wide, and substituting z = q^3/(q^2+1) displaces q^{*} by 2.55 \times 10^{-4}.

Two consequences follow. First, the 80.3\% placement is specific to z = 1/(\sqrt{q} + 1/\sqrt{q}) and does not carry over to z = q^3/(q^2+1), where re-deriving the c_3 ladder is separate work. Second, the skeptical conclusion of this remark is unaffected, and is strengthened: the 80.3\% is a reading of \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)'s own value rather than independent evidence, and at z = q^3/(q^2+1) the root falls outside the anchor interval altogether. The exclusion argument is likewise untouched: its root-monotonicity and root-uniqueness statements concern an abstract \Phi assumed strictly monotone on the anchor interval without reference to z or \alpha, and the numerical premise holds for both parameters (\Phi(q^{*}) \approx -3.606 at z = q^3/(q^2+1) versus -3.631 at z = 1/(\sqrt{q} + 1/\sqrt{q}) — nonzero and of the same sign).

The residual empirical content must be stated with its error bar, because the error bar dominates it. The extractor amplifies the experimental \mathfrak{Q}_\beta uncertainty by 1/u^3, giving \sigma(c_3) = \sigma(\mathfrak{Q}_\beta)/(Q_{N2}u^3) \approx \pm 1.262 — about 61\% of |c_3|. Against that band, c_3's proximity to -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) is 0.031\sigma at the proton anchor and 0.008\sigma at the muon anchor. These are not close agreements in the evidential sense; they are the absence of a measurement, since every candidate constant in [0.807,\, 3.331] agrees at least as well. That interval is 51\times wider than the 0.049 genericity window quoted above, so the window understates the ambiguity by that factor. Distinguishing \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) from a generic in-band constant requires a neutron Q-value sharper by \approx 32\times (proton) or \approx 130\times (muon).

The same arithmetic denies the converse: 0.031\sigma is no evidence against a 4_1-volume ingredient either. Whether the identification is structural remains the open question of Physical role of \mathrm{Im}(q), which this remark interprets; it is settled neither by q^{*} nor by the present precision.

Two calibrating facts sharpen how q^{*} may be used. First, the famous hypersensitivity dc_3/dq \approx 4.7 \times 10^{6} is not a singularity of the underlying object: S'(q^{*}) \approx 2.37 \times (1/u^3), a smooth O(1) prefactor magnified by the 1/u^3 ladder inversion. Second, the precision of q^{*} is limited by the experimental neutron Q-value, dq^{*}/d\mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx -0.539. A sharper \mathfrak{Q}_\beta measurement directly sharpens q^{*}, a concrete falsifiable lever that additional mass anchors at the same \mathfrak{Q}_\beta would not provide.
rem:ohtsuki-tower-bar-parity:
Remark Bar-parity of the Ohtsuki tower at the imaginary aether: even rungs are \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V} (mass), odd rungs are \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} (the bar-odd S). The identification of the bar-odd S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / E_0 with the decay projection \mathrm{Im}(q) (candidate (iii); The \beta-decay S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta/E_0 realizes candidate (iii): a small sign-flipped \mathrm{Im}(q)) has a clean structural counterpart at the level of the figure-eight complex volume \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}. The finite-b (one-loop-plus-corrections) expansion is the Ohtsuki tower

  \mathfrak{V}_b = \mathfrak{V}_0 + \sum_{n \geq 1} \kappa_n\,(2\pi b^2)^n,

with real coefficients \kappa_n \in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{3})\cdot\pi^{\lceil n/2\rceil} (for instance \kappa_1 = 11\sqrt{3}\,\pi/108 and \kappa_2 = 2\pi^2/27). At the aether the fluctuation variable is imaginary: with b = \sqrt{\log q_0 / 2\pi}\,e^{i\pi/4} one has 2\pi b^2 = i\,t, where t = \log q_0 \in \mathbb{R}.

The imaginary aether direction splits the tower by parity, and the split is exactly the \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS} decomposition. Since (i\,t)^2 = -t^2 is real, pairing the imaginary factors gives:

  • even rungs are real — \mathrm{Im}\big((i\,t)^{2m}\,\kappa\big) = 0, so the even sub-tower feeds \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol}, the bar-even (mass) face;
  • odd rungs are imaginary — \mathrm{Re}\big((i\,t)^{2m+1}\,\kappa\big) = 0, so the odd sub-tower feeds \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{CS}, the bar-odd S (decay) face.

Both statements are proved over \mathbb{C}, with the concrete leading rungs \kappa_1 (odd, imaginary) and \kappa_2 (even, real) as instances.

The consequence for the c_3 wall is that the bar-odd S — hence its anchor-dependent sign-flip — lives entirely in the odd (imaginary) sub-tower; the even sub-tower is the anchor-blind volume/mass channel. The odd sub-tower is factorially divergent (Gevrey-1), and its Borel–Padé resummation at the imaginary aether is single-valued: the Borel singularity sits at the real action A = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\pi \approx 0.646 (the geometric-to-conjugate saddle gap), off the imaginary integration ray, so there is no Stokes ambiguity and no exponentially small trans-series. Resurgence therefore returns the exact smooth \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} \approx 0.055 together with the action cross-check, but supplies no anchor-dependent piece. This confirms, from the resummation side, that the S sign-flip is the 1/u^3 ladder representation of a smooth object rather than a physical singularity (compare The \beta-decay S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta/E_0 realizes candidate (iii): a small sign-flipped \mathrm{Im}(q)).

Literature status of the Borel-singularity placement. The principle that Borel singularities of a perturbative quantum invariant sit at complex Chern--Simons values is proved for Seifert fibered homology spheres: for such a closed manifold X, the poles of the Borel transform of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X) coincide, after the normalisation of the Borel variable used there, with the set of classical complex Chern--Simons values \mathrm{CS}_{\mathbb{C}}(X) [andersen-mistegard2020, Thm. 2, §2]. The proof runs through an explicit Laplace-integral representation of Z_0(X) whose integrand is built from the Seifert invariants. The figure-eight complement is hyperbolic, cusped and not Seifert fibered, so the placement of the singularity at \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\pi above is not covered by that theorem. A transfer to S^3\setminus 4_1 would need its own integral representation of the tower and an identification of the singularities of its Borel transform with the complex Chern--Simons values of the geometric and conjugate flat connections; neither is supplied here, and the placement is used as a working statement.

A second, distinct instance of the same bar-parity principle — the deuteron binding. The rung-parity split above is one realisation of "bar involution splits the object by parity"; the deuteron binding correction realises the same principle on a different object — the Frobenius-paired Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_D) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash 6} w_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda_q(\beta_D) over the eleven Wedderburn blocks of H_6(q) (not the figure-eight complex-volume tower). Here the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} acts on the per-block term T_\lambda(q) = w_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda_q(\beta_D) by a signed partition conjugation \lambda \mapsto \lambda' (Young-diagram transpose). Three exact facts pin it: the Markov weight is conjugation-invariant, w_\lambda(q) = w_{\lambda'}(q) (the hook multiset is preserved under transpose); partition conjugation is the bar involution on characters, \chi^{\lambda'}(\beta_D; q) = \chi^\lambda(\beta_D; q^{-1}) (verified against the derived q_0/q_0^{-1} caches); and the weight carries its own bar-sign w_\lambda(q^{-1}) = (-1)^{n-1} w_\lambda(q) from the (q-q^{-1})^{n-1} prefactor. Together these give T_\lambda(q^{-1}) = (-1)^{n-1} T_{\lambda'}(q), and for the deuteron n = 6 the sign is (-1)^5 = -1. For n = 6 the eleven partitions form five conjugate pairs plus the single self-conjugate (3,2,1), and — because of that -1 — the self-conjugate block is bar-odd: T_{(3,2,1)}(q^{-1}) = -T_{(3,2,1)}(q), so it contributes only to the bar-odd impurity t, never to the bar-even coefficient g_2. Equivalently, g_2 is carried by the conjugate-pair asymmetries \Delta_\lambda - \Delta_{\lambda'} (which vanish on the self-conjugate), and t by the pair-symmetric parts plus (3,2,1). The parity backbone is proved over a generic commutative ring; the derivation establishes the structure (signed parity) of the correction only — the per-partition \Delta_\lambda magnitudes remain the open Track-A gate.
prop:one-loop-prefactor-provenance:
Proposition The 1-loop prefactor law splits: the exponent -1/2 is normalisation-invariant and measured, and the constant k = 2^{-1/2} is forced by the saddle condition rather than calibrated on 4_1. Write the sub-leading constant of the volume-conjecture asymptotic as a power law in the Dimofte–Garoufalidis 1-loop invariant,

  c_\sigma \;=\; k \cdot |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}|^{\,p}.

Then the two factors have different provenance.

  • The form is literature. Dimofte–Gukov–Lenells–Zagier expand the perturbative \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) Chern–Simons partition function as Z^{(\rho)}(M;\hbar) = \exp\big(S_0/\hbar - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta^{(\rho)}\log\hbar + \sum_{n\ge 0} S_{n+1}\hbar^n\big) and identify the one-loop coefficient with the Ray–Singer torsion of M twisted by the flat bundle E_\rho: S_1^{(\rho)} = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\big(T(M;E_\rho)/2\big). The statement is for a general 3-manifold with a flat G_\mathbb{C} bundle — no restriction to knots, to two-bridge knots, or to cusp number. So the dependence c_\sigma \propto (\text{torsion})^{-1/2} is not an assumption of this corpus; it is a cited result. What it is not is a theorem: it is a one-loop saddle-point/Feynman-diagram derivation.

  • The exponent is normalisation-invariant, hence measurable. Rescaling c_\sigma \mapsto A\,c_\sigma by any nonzero constant leaves the two-point exponent p_{ij} = (\log c_i - \log c_j)/(\log \tau_i - \log \tau_j) unchanged. Every convention offset is such an A, so no change of convention can move p.

  • And p = -1/2 was already measured, by checks that were read as measuring something else. For any pair of manifolds, c_1\sqrt{\tau_1} = c_2\sqrt{\tau_2} \iff p_{12} = -1/2. The corpus validated the law by checking that k_c := c_\sigma|\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}|^{1/2} agrees across manifolds and recorded the exponent as assumed; those are the same statement. The 17-digit agreement k_1 = k_2 between 4_1 and the Whitehead link is the measurement p = -1/2 to 17 digits.

  • The constant cannot be lifted from DGLZ — but it need not be. DGLZ carry at least three distinct additive offsets between conventions — the /2 inside their logarithm, a +\log 2 relating S_1 to the colored-Jones coefficient s_1, and a \log\pi shift against Gukov–Murakami — and fix their integration constants "by comparison to the asymptotics of the colored Jones polynomial". They calibrate too. So k = 2^{-1/2} cannot be read off their formula. It does not have to be: it is now derived directly from the colored Jones, at both legs, with no convention to reconcile at all.

  • And k = 2^{-1/2} is forced by the saddle condition, before any manifold is named. Laplace's method on a state-sum whose logarithm expands as -(2N/\pi)\Lambda(\theta) + \log(2N\sin\theta) produces three quantities: the saddle condition \Lambda'(\theta) = -\log(2\sin\theta) = 0, i.e. 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1; the Stirling factor 2\sin\theta^\ast; and the Hessian |\Lambda''(\theta^\ast)| = |\cot\theta^\ast|. These give c_\sigma = 2\sin\theta^\ast\,|\cot\theta^\ast|^{-1/2} and |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| = |\cot\theta^\ast|/2 — so in k := c_\sigma|\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}|^{1/2} the Hessian cancels before it is ever evaluated, leaving k^2 = (2\sin\theta^\ast)^2/2 = 1/2. No trace field, no cusp number, no choice of manifold enters. The 4_1 calibration was never carrying information.

The N-power is theorem-backed at two and three cusps. The extraction c_\sigma := \lim_N |J'_N|\,N^{-3/2}e^{-\mathrm{Vol}\cdot N/2\pi} uses the same power 3/2 at every cusp number. Van der Veen proves, for the Whitehead-chain family W_{a,b,c,d}, that J_N \sim \exp\big(\tfrac{1}{2\pi}[(\mathrm{Vol}+i\,\mathrm{CS})N + D\log N + E]\big) with D = 3\pi whenever b = 1 — a value independent of c and d, hence of the number of components. The Whitehead link is W_{0,1,1,0} and the Borromean rings are W_{0,1,1,1}, both with b = 1, so both carry N^{3/2}. The cusp-independence of the exponent is therefore proved for exactly the links this corpus uses, and not merely fitted. The mechanism is Lemma 3's constant: \tilde S_N \sim e^{4N\Lambda(\pi/4)/\pi}(2N)^{-1/2} contributes N^{-(c+d)/2} against Lemma 4's N^{(c+d+3)/2}, and the cusp-dependence cancels exactly.

On the link side the constant is derived, not calibrated. Van der Veen's E is the object measured here as c_\sigma, and his proof gives it explicitly as a (c+d+1)-dimensional Gaussian integral for the whole family; he evaluates it only far enough to show it is nonzero, and his closing paragraph defers the rest — citing the conjecture of Gukov–Murakami that E "is determined by the Ray-Singer torsion of the complement twisted by the holonomy representation" — to a subsequent publication he never wrote. Evaluating that integral, after correcting a sign in his Lemma 2a and one in his Step-3 Gaussian coefficient (neither affecting his theorem), gives in closed form for every b = 1 chain

  c_\sigma\big(W_{a,1,c,d}\big) \;=\; 2^{\,1/2 - n}\,\big(n^2 + m^2\big)^{-1/4},
  \qquad n := c+d,\quad m := 4a - c + d .

Combined with the law, this forces |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| = 2^{\,2n-2}\sqrt{n^2+m^2}. That is a prediction, not a fit: it reproduces the corpus's independently computed |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| at the Whitehead link and the Borromean rings exactly, and it was stated in advance and then confirmed to 18 digits at three further chains the corpus had never touched — L8n5 at three cusps, L10n100 and L10n103 at four. So k = 2^{-1/2} survives a test at a cusp number it was never fitted to, against machinery that knows nothing about the colored Jones polynomial.

Squaring leaves no radical: \tau^2 = 16^{\,n-1}(n^2+m^2), so every b=1 chain has integer \tau^2, and n^2+m^2 is the norm of the Gaussian integer n-mi. The a-dependence is the sharpest part of this, because a enters van der Veen's Lemma 1 only through the phase \chi^{4a-c+d} — the modulus of the summand does not know about it, so the entire a-dependence of |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| is manufactured by interference in the n-sum. Since \mathrm{Vol} is independent of a, the twisted chains are one complement reframed, and framing by \mu-a\lambda on one cusp gives \tau^2 = 2, 10, 26, 50, 82 at two cusps and 64, 320, 320, 1088, 1088 at three — 25 framings, no mismatch, with the three-cusp values coming out equal on every cusp and symmetric under a\mapsto-a, neither of which was put in.

The knot side closes by the same method, and needs no link at all. A b=1 Whitehead chain has c+d+1 \ge 2 components, so nothing above reaches 4_1. But what made the link computation close was not van der Veen: it was that his critical point sits at (\pi/2, \pi/4), a rational point, because those complements are glued from regular ideal octahedra. The figure-eight is two regular ideal tetrahedra, and Kashaev's invariant \langle 4_1\rangle_N = \sum_k |(q;q)_k|^2 = \sum_k e^{-2s_k} is a one-variable sum in the same s_k. Its saddle is at \theta^\ast = 5\pi/6, the Stirling factor is 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1, the Hessian is |\cot\theta^\ast| = \sqrt3, and

  \langle 4_1\rangle_N \;\sim\; 3^{-1/4}\,N^{3/2}\,e^{\mathrm{Vol}\cdot N/2\pi},

so c_\sigma(4_1) = 3^{-1/4} and the power 3/2 are both derived. In one variable the saddle condition is 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1, so the Stirling factor is pinned to 1 and c_\sigma = |\cot\theta^\ast|^{-1/2} = 3^{-1/4} with no freedom: 3^{-1/4} is a property of one summation variable, not of 4_1. The 4_1 calibration on which the whole c_\sigma arc rested is thereby retired.

Where closed forms exist, and why there are exactly two. The saddle sits at a root-of-unity shape precisely for the regular ideal polyhedra — z = e^{i\pi/3} (tetrahedron, trace field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3) = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}), |\tau| = \sqrt3/2) and z = i (octahedron, trace field \mathbb{Q}(i), |\tau| = 2^{2n-2}|A| with A = n - mi a Gaussian integer and |A| = \sqrt{n^2+m^2} the root of its norm). Those are the two imaginary quadratic fields with extra units, the two Bianchi cases. For a general knot the trace field is a general number field and \det(\mathrm{Hess}) — which is what \tau_{\mathrm{DG}} is — is an algebraic number in it with no reason to admit a radical expression. The obstruction to extending the method is arithmetic, not analytic.

What remains open, stated exactly. The law itself: what is established is that a derived Jones-side constant and an independently computed 1-loop invariant satisfy c_\sigma \propto |\tau|^{-1/2} on six manifolds at one, two, three and four cusps, which is a far stronger test than the corpus previously had and is still not a proof. The analytic input — the Euler–Maclaurin expansion of s_k and Laplace's method — is now established, but not yet connected: the statements above still assume the saddle as hypotheses and prove the algebra downstream, which is where the rigidity lives. Both inputs are proved separately. The first gives the expansion with an explicit remainder, \log g_k = -\tfrac{2N}{\pi}\Lambda(\theta) + \log(2N\sin\theta) + \tfrac{\pi}{6N}\cot\theta + O(1/N^2), its constant term derived from \Lambda(b) = b - b\log 2b + O(b^3) rather than fitted; the second gives Laplace's method for the sum as an exact Jacobi-theta identity, so sum and integral agree to 1 + O(e^{-\pi^2/a}). What is still assumed is the step from those two theorems to the saddle hypotheses on c_\sigma and \tau — extracting the saddle condition, the Stirling factor and the Hessian from the expansion. That is a smaller and much better-defined gap than the two it replaced, and it is the one to state when citing this proposition.

The distinction the proposition draws also fixes the shape of the residual risk. Any missing cusp-dependent step g in the dictionary between the two normalisations satisfies k_{\mathrm{meas}}(c) = k_{\mathrm{true}}\,g(c), so agreement of the measured constants at two cusp numbers forces g to agree there — which excludes every candidate with g(1)\neq g(2), the retracted per-cusp factor 2^{(c-1)/2} among them. On the character-variety side, Léo Bénard [benard2018, Ch. 2, §2.3.1, §2.4] realises adjoint Reidemeister torsion as a rational form on the character variety controlled at finite points through the Alexander polynomial with a separate analysis at ideal points, supplying the variety-level normalisation framework in which any general-c cusp factor would have to be checked across arbitrary cusp count c rather than inferred from c \in \{1, 2, 3\}. The tension lives in the exponent bookkeeping, not in the constant, at the cusp numbers tested.
rem:adjoint-torsion-derivative-duality-p:
Remark Prior art: the adjoint torsion as a derivative, with a signed duality. Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold whose boundary is b tori, \rho an irreducible \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})-representation on the geometric component, and \varphi\colon \pi_1(M) \to \mathbb{Z}^n a surjection. Dubois and Yamaguchi define the twisted Alexander invariant \Delta^{\varphi \otimes \mathrm{Ad}\circ\rho}_M as the torsion of an acyclic complex, show that it is a Laurent polynomial up to a monomial factor, and prove that its limit at t_1, \ldots, t_n \to 1, divided by one factor t^{a^{(\ell)}} - 1 per boundary torus, is (-1)^b times the non-abelian (adjoint) Reidemeister torsion \mathbb{T}^M_\lambda(\rho) [dubois-yamaguchi2012, \S 1, p. 2]. They also prove a signed duality: for a link exterior,

\Delta^{\varphi \otimes \mathrm{Ad}\circ\rho}_{E_L}(t^{-1}) = (-1)^b\, \Delta^{\varphi \otimes \mathrm{Ad}\circ\rho}_{E_L}(t)

up to a factor t^k, so that for a knot exterior the polynomial is odd under t \mapsto t^{-1} [dubois-yamaguchi2012, Theorem 14 and eqs. (32)--(33), \S 8, p. 23]. For the Whitehead link exterior at a lift of the holonomy representation and its conjugate they obtain \mathbb{T}^{E_L}_\lambda = \tau_0 \cdot 8(1 \mp \sqrt{-1}), with \tau_0 = \pm 1 a sign [dubois-yamaguchi2012, \S 6.3, eq. (29), p. 19].

This gives the 1-loop prefactor proposition a second, independent way to compute the torsion it uses, through an acyclic complex rather than a triangulation. Because the torsion is a topological invariant, any formula for it that changes value when the same manifold is retriangulated is a defect of that formula, not evidence that the quantity is ill-defined. The duality is a checkable constraint on any torsion polynomial the corpus produces.

The normalisations have not been reconciled. At the Whitehead link the proposition's closed form gives |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| = \sqrt{2}, while the value above has modulus 8\sqrt{2}, for the curve fixed by their substitution t_1 = t_2 = t. Which choice of curve and which convention factor account for the ratio 8 has not been worked out here, so the two numbers should not be used interchangeably.
conj:stokes-dt-bps-bridge:
Conjecture Resurgent Stokes constants are Donaldson--Thomas / BPS degeneracies (the closed-sector state-integral bridge, GGM Conjecture 3(d) + GPPV). For a hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the resurgent Stokes constant of the state integral of S^3 \setminus K on its distinguished (geometric Borel) ray is a Donaldson--Thomas invariant / BPS degeneracy of the associated 3d \mathcal{N}=2 theory T[K]:

  \mathfrak{S}(K) \;=\; \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) \;=\; \dim \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]),

where \mathfrak{S}(K) is the Stokes constant, \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) the Donaldson--Thomas / Kontsevich--Soibelman invariant of the q-difference structure, and \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]) the space of BPS states whose graded dimension categorifies the 3d index.

For the general setting of the middle term: a BPS structure (Z, \Gamma, \Omega) carries Donaldson--Thomas invariants \Omega(\gamma), and to it is attached a Riemann--Hilbert problem [bridgeland2016, §2, §4]. For finite, uncoupled, integral BPS structures that problem has an explicit solution in products of gamma functions [bridgeland2016, §3.2]. The knot BPS structures in this conjecture are not shown to be uncoupled, so that result is context, not a case of the conjecture. On the state-integral side, one-dimensional state integrals of products of Faddeev quantum dilogarithms, including those of 4_1 and 5_2, are finite sums of products of a q-series and a \tilde q-series, and the generating q-series is admissible in the sense of Kontsevich--Soibelman [garoufalidis2013, §1.1, §1.3--1.4]. The theorem there is proved for a family of one-dimensional state integrals; the multi-dimensional statement is described as well known to experts but is not proved in that source, so any use of the factorisation beyond one-dimensional integrals rests on the unproved case [garoufalidis2013, §1.1]. The same one-dimensional state integrals have been evaluated at rational points, that is at q a root of unity, in terms of the Rogers dilogarithm, the cyclic quantum dilogarithm and truncated state sums [garoufalidis-kashaev2015, §1.1]. The aether value q_0 is real and greater than 1, not a root of unity, so those evaluations bear on the fibre-level state integral and not directly on its archimedean evaluation at q_0; a numerical agreement there would be a cross-check, not an input.

The first equality is [garoufalidis-gu-marino2023peacock] Conjecture 3(d) — "the Stokes constants are integers corresponding to the Donaldson--Thomas invariants and the BPS degeneracies" — which Garoufalidis--Gu--Mariño state as a conjecture and do not prove for any knot, 4_1 included. What they prove is their Conjecture 5 for 4_1 and 5_2 (their Theorem 6, via Theorems 17 and 25), and they verify Conjecture 4 for both knots by computation (§5.2, §6.2). The second is the [gukov-pei-putrov-vafa2017] (GPPV) realisation of the DT/BPS count as the graded dimension of the fivebrane BPS Hilbert space of T[M_3] on M_3 \times D^2, categorifying the 3d \mathcal{N}=2 indices. prop:residue-at-root:
Proposition Cyclotomic residues of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} — algebraic definition. Let T_w \in J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} have \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) \in \mathbb{Q}(q), and suppose \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) lies in the Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. The cyclotomic residue

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}(\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell})(T_w)

is the image of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) under the cyclotomic projection

  \pi_{n_\ell}
  \;:\;
  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}
  \longrightarrow
  \mathbb{Z}[q] / \Phi_{n_\ell}(q),

evaluating identically within the residue field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_\ell).

The cyclotomic residue is defined purely algebraically within the Habiro completion of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. It avoids complex-analytic limits entirely. The formulation keeps the algebraic sector strictly within \mathbb{Q}-coefficients, fulfilling the three-calibration discipline.

The cyclotomic projection \pi_n is constructed: \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is the ring of compatible threads in \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_N, N \ge 0, and \pi_n reads off the level-n class and reduces it modulo \Phi_n(q), which divides 1 - q^n and hence (q;q)_n. It is a ring homomorphism, and on a polynomial it is reduction modulo \Phi_n(q). The residue of a product is therefore the product of the residues.

The hypothesis that \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) lies in \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is not proved here. That membership, together with the reality of the residue and its dependence only on the class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q), is the open content of Existence of the cyclotomic residue at each filtration level.
prf:residue-at-root:
Proof Proof of residue at root. The Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is realised as the ring of threads (x_N)_{N \ge 0}, x_N \in \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_N with (q;q)_N = \prod_{k=1}^{N}(1 - q^k), compatible under the reductions \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_M \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_N for N \le M. These reductions exist because (q;q)_N divides (q;q)_M. Compatibility is preserved by sums and products, so the threads form a subring of the product.

For n \ge 1 the cyclotomic polynomial \Phi_n(q) divides 1 - q^n, which is a factor of (q;q)_n. Reduction modulo \Phi_n(q) therefore factors through \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_n, and

  \pi_n(x) \;:=\; x_n \bmod \Phi_n(q)
  \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q)

defines a ring homomorphism \pi_n : \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q). On the constant thread of a polynomial p, \pi_n returns the class of p, so \pi_n is surjective and restricts to the usual reduction on \mathbb{Z}[q].

By hypothesis, \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) is an element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. Applying \pi_{n_\ell} and identifying \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_{n_\ell}(q) with \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_\ell] gives the residue, an element of the cyclotomic ring. Because \pi_{n_\ell} is a ring homomorphism, the residue of a sum or product is the sum or product of the residues. \blacksquare

The construction does not use analytic continuation. Habiro shows that, for elements of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}, these projections agree with evaluation at roots of unity [habiro2004, §1.2]; that comparison is not needed for the statement.
prf:graded-markov-trace-from-gs-filtrati:

  \mathrm{pairs}_n
  \;=\;

    \Phi_q\!\bigl(\bigl|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}\bigr|\bigr),

rem:jet-tower-convergence-context:
Remark Boundedness hypothesis, engineering consequence, and confinement-SDP relation for jet-tower convergence. On the hypothesis.

The hypothesis |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)| \leq \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) — uniform boundedness of per-level binding across the brane tower — is the named conjecture uniform per-level binding bound. This proposition therefore reduces the convergence question to a single boundedness statement: once \Delta^{(n)} is shown to be bounded (uniformly or with growth slower than \hbar_q^{-2n}), the tail decays as a geometric series.

prop:full-pole-structure-mass-trace:
Proposition Cyclotomic expansion of the cleared mass trace. Let T_w \in H_n(q) be a standard basis element, with the Markov trace at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and h = q - q^{-1}. Then:

  1. By the Hecke-algebra Markov-trace structure of V. F. R. Jones [jones1987], \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) is a polynomial in z of degree at most n-1 with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[h]. Hence the cleared numerator
  N(T_w) \;:=\; (q^{2}+1)^{\,n-1}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].
  1. N(T_w) lies in the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} := \varprojlim_m \mathbb{Z}[q]/((q;q)_m) of Kazuo Habiro [habiro2004cyclotomic] (applied to unified Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants in [habiro2008]), in which q is a unit, and expands cyclotomically as
  N(T_w)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{m \geq 0} a_m(T_w)\,(q; q)_m .
  1. The trace itself is not in general an element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. For T_w = \sigma_1 \in H_2(q), \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z satisfies (1+q^{2})\,z = q^{3}, and evaluating at q = i (a ring map \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[i]) would give 0 = -i.

The primitive roots of unity populate S^1 densely, blocking any complex-analytic continuation across the boundary. The Habiro ring provides the algebraic layer for the cleared numerator, not for the trace: the factor (q^{2}+1)^{-(n-1)} has poles at q = \pm i, and only after removing it does evaluation at every root of unity make sense.
prf:full-pole-structure-mass-trace:
Proof Proof of full pole structure mass trace. Part 1. Induct on n. On H_1(q) = R the trace is \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1. For w \in S_{n+1} \setminus S_n the coset decomposition gives T_w = T_u\,\sigma_n\,T_v with u, v \in S_n, so the Markov property and cyclicity give \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(T_v T_u). The product T_v T_u expands in the standard basis of H_n(q) with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[h], because the only relation used is \sigma_i^{2} = h\,\sigma_i + 1. By induction each \mathrm{tr}_M(T_x), x \in S_n, is a polynomial in z of degree at most n-1 over \mathbb{Z}[h], so \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) has degree at most n. For w \in S_n the induction hypothesis applies directly. Since h \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] and (q^{2}+1)z = q^{3}, multiplying by (q^{2}+1)^{n-1} clears every denominator.

Part 2. \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}] \subset \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} because q is a unit there. Sequential division by (1 - q^{m+1}) produces the coefficients a_m (atomic Habiro expansion, Step 2) [habiro2004].

Part 3. Evaluation at a root of unity is a ring homomorphism on \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. If z lay in \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}, applying evaluation at q = i to (1+q^{2})z = q^{3} would give 0 = -i. \square

Inadequacy of the previous wording

Two specific failures of the "meromorphic on \mathbb{C}" picture:

  1. Density on S^1. The set \{\zeta_n^{(j)} : \gcd(j,n)=1, n \geq 2\} is dense in S^1. A meromorphic function on a connected open set has only isolated poles; with poles dense in S^1 the only consistent picture is that S^1 is a natural boundary, and there is no single connected meromorphic continuation across it. The Habiro ring sidesteps this by working in the cyclotomic completion of \mathbb{Z}[q], where evaluation at each root of unity is defined polynomially without any complex-analytic continuation.
  2. Convergence. The Cauchy-kernel partial sum \sum_{n \leq N} \sum_j r_n^{(j)}/(q - \zeta_n^{(j)}) does not converge uniformly on any neighbourhood that crosses S^1. The Habiro expansion converges in the q-adic ((q;q)_\bullet)-topology by construction, and reduces modulo (q;q)_m at every truncation order.

This proposition replaces the earlier "meromorphic with poles at all primitive roots of unity" wording with the algebraically correct Habiro-ring statement; the residue spectral sum (GB residue spectral sum) is retained as the symbolic feeding lemma that produces the cyclotomic coefficients a_m from the Wedderburn-stratum residues r_n^{(j)}, but is no longer claimed to define a global \mathbb{C}-meromorphic function.

prf:habiro-expansion-atomic:
Proof Proof of habiro expansion atomic. The proof is the constructive sequential cyclotomic-division algorithm. The general existence/uniqueness of the cyclotomic expansion (with a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], no termination) is the content of (Habiro completion); the present proof specialises to atomic braids and establishes termination.

Step 1: Integrality of p(u)

The Markov trace on the standard Hecke basis has rational expression in q with cyclotomic denominators: each Markov factor z = u/(u^2+1) contributes (u^2+1)^{-k}, and the Schur–Weyl decomposition (Schur–Weyl) expresses \mathrm{tr}_M via q-hook products [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}), also cyclotomic in u. Markov–Jones integrality [jones1987] Thm 3 gives \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q) \in \mathbb{Z}[u, u^{-1}] \cdot D(u)^{-1}; multiplying by D(u) yields p(u) \in \mathbb{Z}[u, u^{-1}].

Step 2: Sequential cyclotomic division

Define p_0 := p and, for m \geq 0,

  a_m(u) \;:=\; p_m(u) \bmod (1 - u^{m+1}),
  \qquad
  p_{m+1}(u) \;:=\; \frac{p_m(u) - a_m(u)}{1 - u^{m+1}}.

The polynomial 1 - u^{m+1} is monic (up to sign), so polynomial division in \mathbb{Z}[u] produces a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[u] of degree \leq m and a quotient p_{m+1} \in \mathbb{Z}[u]. This gives integrality and the degree bound.

Step 3: Termination

At each step \deg p_{m+1} = \deg p_m - (m+1) + \deg a_m \leq \deg p_m - 1, so \deg p_m is strictly decreasing in any step producing a nonzero a_m. The process terminates after finitely many steps. The total degree gain \sum_{k=0}^m (k+1) = \binom{m+2}{2} then gives m_{\max} \leq \lceil \sqrt{2d} \rceil where d = \deg p.

Step 4: Reconstruction and uniqueness

Unrolling the recursion gives p(u) = \sum_{m \leq m_{\max}} a_m(u)\,(u; u)_m. For uniqueness, at the smallest m where a_m \neq a_m' the polynomial a_m - a_m' would be divisible by 1 - u^{m+1}, but \deg(a_m - a_m') \leq m < m+1 = \deg(1 - u^{m+1}) — contradiction. \square

Remark Per-partition \Delta_\lambda value versus open super-pairwise many-body binding magnitude. The partition weight \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda \in \mathbb{Z} established in DT/3d-index unification of \Delta_\lambda separates an exact combinatorial per-block value from an open many-body extensive binding magnitude. Following the Springer correspondence for a unipotent element of Jordan type \lambda in \mathrm{GL}_n, the top cohomology of the Springer fibre carries the irreducible S_n-module V_\lambda (Tonny A. Springer [springer1976]; Toshiaki Shoji [shoji2019, Thm. 2.1]), explaining the terminology while both the jet-valuation parity (-1)^{n(\lambda)} and the Wedderburn dimension \dim V_\lambda are derived directly within the Hecke aether.

Intensive per-block value versus extensive many-body magnitude. Because the normalized Markov-trace weighted sum \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda(\beta)\,\Delta_\lambda is intensive, no per-partition scalar weight \Delta_\lambda can generate the super-pairwise extensive nuclear binding energy documented in Term 6 binding density. Six distinct ansätze attempting to absorb the light-nuclide magnitude deficit (r^\ast \approx 1.585 at the deuteron) into \Delta_\lambda—Frobenius co-Casimir, Demazure-fibre, LP-Plancherel, LP-Frobenius, level-0 crystal-graph, and augmented-Markov—all fail at A = 2. Furthermore, the pairwise exchange determinant on [0, 1] satisfies (1 - m^2)^6 \le (1 + 3m)(1 - m)^3, capping the four-body pairwise log-determinant cumulant at \rho_4 \le \binom{4}{2} = 6, whereas nuclear {}^4\mathrm{He} binding requires \rho_4 \approx 13 > 6. Any genuine closure of the many-body binding magnitude must therefore arise from an irreducibly super-pairwise (\ge 3-body) extensive mechanism rather than a re-weighting of \Delta_\lambda.

Phenomenological depth-two recurrences are not derivations. Discrete depth-two q-difference recurrences w_{n+1} = a_0 w_n + r_{\mathrm{res}} w_{n-1} on the [n]_q!-normalized carrier (distinct up to scalar gauge from the resurgent Stokes carrier of Stavros Garoufalidis, Jie Gu, and Marcos Mariño [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]) reproduce multi-body binding hierarchies only when seeded with calibrated phenomenological constants (a_0 = 1/2, r_{\mathrm{res}} \approx 2.596, and empirical isospin shifts). Under the three-observable calibration discipline (m_e, \mathfrak{D}_\beta, m_\pi), such seeded recurrences are exploratory fits rather than parameter-free predictions; the parameter-free many-body nuclear binding magnitude remains open.
rem:tjon-universality-external:
Remark The external three-body/four-body correlation, and why it does not license the simplex baseline. The many-body magnitude leg of \Delta_\lambda (Per-partition \Delta_\lambda value versus open super-pairwise many-body binding magnitude) is scored against an external observable—the empirical correlation between three-body and four-body binding energies, known in nuclear physics as the Tjon line. Separating what the effective-field-theory literature establishes from the inclusion--exclusion simplex expansion prevents an analogy from being misread as a derived premise.

The external results

Two results are used.

No four-body parameter at leading order. Working in an effective theory of short-range interactions whose two-body scattering length a is large compared with the natural low-energy length scale \ell of the interaction (|a| \gg \ell), Lucas Platter, Hans-Werner Hammer, and Ulf-G. Meißner find that an \mathrm{SU}(4)-symmetric one-parameter three-nucleon interaction suffices to renormalise the four-nucleon system at leading order in \ell/|a|; the empirical triton--\alpha correlation then follows by varying that single three-body parameter [platter2005tjon]. With the binding energies B({}^2\mathrm{H}) = 2.22\,\mathrm{MeV} and B({}^3\mathrm{H}) = 8.48\,\mathrm{MeV} as inputs they obtain B(\alpha) \approx 29.5\,\mathrm{MeV} for the \alpha-particle, against a Coulomb-corrected experimental 29.0 \pm 0.1\,\mathrm{MeV}.

A dimensionless four-to-three ratio. Solving the four-boson Yakubovsky equations with no four-body parameter, Hans-Werner Hammer and Lucas Platter report that away from threshold the four-body ground state and the deepest three-body state are related by a factor of 5 [hammer2007fourbody]. The correlation is approximately linear away from threshold for either sign of a, with positive curvature for a > 0 and negative curvature for a < 0; the nonlinearity is confined to the threshold region.

Limits of the external results

Each of the following is a separate statement that the results above do not license:

  1. "No four-body parameter is needed" is not "no four-body force exists." The first is a statement about leading-order renormalisation; the second is a statement about physical interactions. The four-nucleon force is small, not absent: Eric D. Jurgenson, Petr Navrátil, and Richard J. Furnstahl evaluate the similarity-renormalisation-group-induced four-body contribution at {}^4\mathrm{He} as a net effect of order tens of keV, with the long-range \mathrm{N}^3\mathrm{LO} estimate of order a few hundred keV [jurgenson2009srg].

  2. The leading-order claim is contested in general. Yamashita et al. find a strong sensitivity of the deepest four-body energy to a four-body subtraction constant, concluding that a four-body parameter should generally enter at leading order. As noted in [hammer2007fourbody], both analyses agree on the nuclear case because short-range repulsion suppresses four-particle contact configurations, while general universality rests on the inherited renormalisation-group power counting.

  3. The zero-range limit is not the nuclear regime. The universal ratio 5 is a zero-range result, whereas experimental nuclear binding from AME2020 [ame2020] gives B({}^4\mathrm{He})/B({}^3\mathrm{H}) \approx 3.42 after Coulomb correction; [platter2005tjon] attributes the shift of its leading-order Tjon line to neglected finite-range effects.

Inequivalence with the simplex condition

Expanding the many-body binding moment in an inclusion--exclusion simplex basis,

  M(A) \;=\; \sum_k \mu_k \binom{A}{k},

translates the naive ansatz \mu_4 = 0 into M(4) = 4M(3) - 6M(2). That algebraic condition is provably inequivalent to leading-order three-body renormalisability. On the \mu_4 = 0 baseline, M(4) < 4\,M(3) holds strictly for every \mu_2 > 0 and arbitrary \mu_3 (with deficit -6\mu_2), placing the universal zero-range ratio M(4)/M(3) = 5 outside the reachable cone. Conversely, substituting M(4) = 5\,M(3) forces

  \mu_4 \;=\; 9\mu_2 + \mu_3,

so \mu_4 is largest precisely in a four-boson calculation carrying zero four-body interaction input. Because three moments fitted to three anchors (A = 2, 3, 4) determine an exact algebraic identity

  \mu_4 \;:=\; M(4) - 4M(3) + 6M(2),

\mu_4 measures only the departure of M(4) from the two-point binomial extrapolation, not an irreducible physical four-body potential. The external Tjon-line literature therefore motivates tracking departures from two-point extrapolation, without deriving the simplex baseline or licensing a four-body force interpretation of \mu_4.
